tool.help:
.. class:: infomark
**What this tool does**
This tool computes **spin-up period metadata** for long-term soil organic carbon (SOC) model simulations. It reads a table of experimental site descriptions and, for each site, determines the optimal dates for the model initialization (spin-up) phase — that is, the period of climate data to use to bring the carbon pools to a steady state before the forward simulation begins.
The output is a metadata table listing the spin-up start and end dates, the effective duration, and a plain-language description of the strategy applied. This table can then be passed to a dedicated climate data extraction tool (GEOSAS/SAFRAN or Open-Meteo/ERA5).
The **Target climate data source** parameter controls which reanalysis will be used downstream and therefore sets the earliest date from which data can be requested:
* **GEOSAS / SAFRAN** — French meteorological reanalysis (Météo-France / INRAE GEOSAS). Available from **1959-01-01**. * **Open-Meteo / ERA5** — Global ERA5 and ERA5-Land reanalysis. Available worldwide from **1940-01-01**.
-----
**Input: Site metadata CSV**
Comma-separated file. The tool only reads two date columns, picked with the **First measurement date column** and **Last measurement date column** dropdowns, which are populated from the columns of the uploaded file. Any other columns are passed through untouched.
+---------------------------------+-------------------------------------------------------------+ | Column (selected via dropdown) | Description | +==================================+=============================================================+ | First measurement date column | Year (YYYY) or date (YYYYMMDD) of the first SOC measurement | +---------------------------------+-------------------------------------------------------------+ | Last measurement date column | Year (YYYY) or date (YYYYMMDD) of the last SOC measurement | +---------------------------------+-------------------------------------------------------------+
A ``site_name`` column is also required in the input file.
-----
**Spin-up period logic**
For each site:
1. **Target start** = first measurement date − ``spinup_target_years`` 2. Clip to the **earliest date** available in the chosen reanalysis (``1959-01-01`` for SAFRAN, ``1940-01-01`` for ERA5). 3. **Effective spin-up duration** (years) = first measurement date − clipped start. 4. If effective duration ≥ ``spinup_min_years``:
* Spin-up = [clipped start → first measurement date] *(pre-experiment period)*
5. If effective duration < ``spinup_min_years``:
* Spin-up = [clipped start → clipped start + ``spinup_target_years``] *(first N years of the experiment used instead)*
-----
**Output — Spin-up metadata CSV**
One row per site:
+---------------------------+----------------------------------------------------------+ | Column | Description | +===========================+==========================================================+ | ``site_name`` | Site identifier | +---------------------------+----------------------------------------------------------+ | ``begin_date`` | Date of the first SOC measurement | +---------------------------+----------------------------------------------------------+ | ``end_date`` | Date of the last SOC measurement | +---------------------------+----------------------------------------------------------+ | ``start_spinup`` | First day of the spin-up period | +---------------------------+----------------------------------------------------------+ | ``end_spinup`` | Last day of the spin-up period | +---------------------------+----------------------------------------------------------+ | ``spinup_duration_yr`` | Effective spin-up duration (years) | +---------------------------+----------------------------------------------------------+ | ``method_spinup`` | Description of the spin-up strategy applied | +---------------------------+----------------------------------------------------------+ | ``api_source`` | Target reanalysis (``geosas`` or ``openmeteo``) | +---------------------------+----------------------------------------------------------+
Note: in the output, the two date columns are always written back using the canonical names ``begin_date`` and ``end_date``, regardless of which input columns were selected.
-----
**References**

(2020). The ERA5 global reanalysis. *Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society*, 146(730), 1999–2049. https://doi.org/10.1002/qj.3803 * Open-Meteo API documentation: https://open-meteo.com/en/docs/historical-weather-api * GEOSAS API documentation: https://geosas.fr/web/?page_id=6345
